title: Array Find: First Even Number
description: Given an array of numbers nums, use Array.prototype.find to return the first even number. If no even number exists, return undefined.
whatShouldHappen: The callback returns true if num % 2 === 0.
Return the found even number or undefined.
patternExplanation: .find() stops at the first element matching a predicate function, avoiding unnecessary iterations.

title: Array FindIndex: First Negative Value
description: Given an array of numbers nums, use Array.prototype.findIndex to return the 0-based index of the first negative number. Return -1 if no negative number is present.
patternExplanation: .findIndex() locates the position of an element based on a dynamic condition rather than exact primitive equality.

title: Array FindLast: Last Odd Number
description: Given an array of integers nums, use Array.prototype.findLast to find the last odd number (Math.abs(n) % 2 === 1). Return undefined if none is found.
whatShouldHappen: Return the last matching odd number.
patternExplanation: .findLast() iterates backwards from the end of the array, returning the rightmost match without reversing the array.

title: Array FindLastIndex: Last Target Occurrence
description: Given an array of strings words and a target string target, use Array.prototype.findLastIndex to return the last index where word === target. Return -1 if not found.
whatShouldHappen: Return the index of the rightmost match or -1.
patternExplanation: .findLastIndex() finds the index of the last element satisfying a predicate function.

title: Array IndexOf with FromIndex Offset
description: Given an array items, a target value target, and a starting offset fromIndex, use items.indexOf(target, fromIndex) to search for target starting from fromIndex. Return the index or -1.
patternExplanation: Providing the optional fromIndex argument to indexOf ignores earlier occurrences and begins the forward search at a specified position.

title: Array Flat: Single Level Flatten
description: Given an array arr containing nested sub-arrays, use Array.prototype.flat() to flatten it by one depth level.
patternExplanation: .flat(1) concatenates sub-array elements up to specified depth into a new array.

title: Array Flat: Multi-Level Depth
description: Given an array arr and a depth integer depth, use arr.flat(depth) to flatten nested arrays up to depth levels deep.
patternExplanation: Passing an explicit depth parameter controls recursion depth when flattening multi-level arrays.

title: Array FlatMap: Split Sentences into Words
description: Given an array of sentence strings sentences, use Array.prototype.flatMap to split each sentence by spaces (' ') and return a single flat array of words.
whatShouldHappen: Return the flat list of words.
patternExplanation: .flatMap() maps each item to an array and flattens the result by one level, equivalent to .map().flat(1) but in a single efficient pass.

title: Array FlatMap: Duplicate Even Numbers
description: Given an array of numbers nums, use Array.prototype.flatMap to return a new array where even numbers appear duplicated ([n, n]) and odd numbers appear once ([n]).
patternExplanation: .flatMap() allows mapping 1 element to 0, 1, or multiple elements, dynamically expanding or shrinking arrays.

title: Array.from: Generate Integer Sequence
description: Given length and startVal, use Array.from({ length }, (_, i) => startVal + i) to generate an array of sequential integers starting from startVal.
whatShouldHappen: Call Array.from({ length }, (_, i) => startVal + i).
patternExplanation: Array.from with an array-like object { length } and a mapping function constructs sequences without manual loop pushes.

title: Array Every: All Numbers Positive
description: Given an array of numbers nums, use Array.prototype.every to check if every number is strictly greater than 0. Return true if all are positive (or if the array is empty), otherwise false.
patternExplanation: .every() returns true only if the callback returns truthy for all elements, short-circuiting on the first falsy result.

title: Array Some: Divisible by Divisor
description: Given an array of numbers nums and an integer k, use Array.prototype.some to check if at least one number in nums is divisible by k (n % k === 0). Return boolean.
whatShouldHappen: Return true if any element satisfies the condition, else false.
patternExplanation: .some() returns true as soon as any element satisfies the predicate, avoiding inspecting the rest of the array.

title: Array Includes with Starting Offset
description: Given an array arr, a searchElement, and a fromIndex integer, return whether arr.includes(searchElement, fromIndex) is true.
patternExplanation: Using the secondary index parameter of includes restricts lookup to elements at or after the given position.

title: Array.isArray: Count Sub-Arrays
description: Given an array items containing mixed elements, use Array.isArray to count how many elements are themselves arrays.
whatShouldHappen: Return the length of the filtered array.
patternExplanation: Array.isArray() is the reliable standard way to verify array types, avoiding false positives from typeof returning "object".

title: Array Every: All Strings Non-Empty
description: Given an array arr, use Array.prototype.every to check if every element is both of type "string" and has length > 0. Return boolean.
patternExplanation: Combining typeof with length validation inside .every() ensures schema compliance across collections.

title: Array toSorted: Ascending Numeric Order
description: Given an array of numbers nums, use Array.prototype.toSorted((a, b) => a - b) to return a new sorted copy in ascending order without modifying nums.
patternExplanation: .toSorted() sorts an array immutably, returning a newly created copy and leaving the original array intact.

title: Array toReversed: Immutable Reverse
description: Given an array arr, use Array.prototype.toReversed() to return a new array with elements in reversed order without mutating arr.
patternExplanation: .toReversed() creates a reversed copy without the side-effects of in-place .reverse().

title: Array toSpliced: Remove Elements Immutably
description: Given an array arr, a start index, and deleteCount, use arr.toSpliced(start, deleteCount) to return a new array with those elements removed without mutating arr.
patternExplanation: .toSpliced() performs splice insertions and deletions immutably, preserving state purity.

title: Array with: Replace Value at Index
description: Given an array arr, an index, and a newVal, use arr.with(index, newVal) to return a new array with the element at index replaced, without modifying arr.
patternExplanation: .with(index, value) replaces a single item by index immutably in a concise single statement.

title: Array toSorted: Descending Numeric Order
description: Given an array of numbers nums, use Array.prototype.toSorted((a, b) => b - a) to return a new sorted copy in descending order without mutating nums.
patternExplanation: Using (a, b) => b - a reverses comparator precedence to achieve descending order.

title: Reduce: Product of All Numbers
description: Given an array of numbers nums, use Array.prototype.reduce with initial value 1 to return the product of all elements. For empty array, return 1.
patternExplanation: Starting a reduce accumulator at 1 produces the total product across array elements.

title: Array reduceRight: Reverse String Concatenation
description: Given an array of strings words, use Array.prototype.reduceRight to concatenate words in right-to-left order into a single string.
patternExplanation: .reduceRight() processes elements from right to left, useful for reverse traversals and right-associative operations.

title: Reduce: Find Maximum Number
description: Given a non-empty array of numbers nums, use Array.prototype.reduce to find the maximum value without using Math.max.
whatShouldHappen: Call nums.reduce((max, n) => n > max ? n : max, nums[0]).
patternExplanation: Comparing each element with the running accumulator in reduce tracks the extremum in single-pass O(n) time.

title: Reduce: Partition Numbers by Parity
description: Given an array of integers nums, use Array.prototype.reduce to partition them into an object { evens: number[], odds: number[] }.
whatShouldHappen: If n % 2 === 0, push to acc.evens, else push to acc.odds.
patternExplanation: Using an object of arrays as the accumulator partitions a dataset into categories in one traversal.

title: Reduce: Map Words to Lengths Object
description: Given an array of strings words, use Array.prototype.reduce to construct an object where each key is a word and its value is the length of that word.
whatShouldHappen: Call words.reduce((acc, word) => { acc[word] = word.length; return acc; }, {}).
patternExplanation: Building dictionary mappings from arrays using .reduce() transforms flat collections into key-value property lookups.

title: Array Slice: Take First N Elements
description: Given an array arr and integer n, use arr.slice(0, n) to return the first n elements. If n <= 0, return [].
patternExplanation: .slice(0, n) safely extracts the head of an array without altering the original array.

title: Array Slice: Drop First N Elements
description: Given an array arr and integer n, use arr.slice(n) to return all elements after skipping the first n items.
whatShouldHappen: Return the tail of the array.
patternExplanation: Calling .slice(n) with a single positive argument drops the initial n items.

title: Array Slice: Extract Last K Items
description: Given an array arr and integer k, use arr.slice(-k) to return the last k elements. If k <= 0, return [].
patternExplanation: Negative index arguments in .slice() count from the end of the array, cleanly extracting trailing elements.

title: Array Slice: Subarray Between Indices
description: Given an array arr and two non-negative indices startIdx and endIdx, use arr.slice(startIdx, endIdx) to return the elements from startIdx up to (not including) endIdx.
patternExplanation: .slice(start, end) creates a shallow slice bounded by [start, end) without mutating input.

title: Array Slice: Chunk into Pairs
description: Given an array arr, use a loop with arr.slice(i, i + 2) to partition arr into pairs of 2 elements. If the last chunk has only 1 element, include it as a single-element array.
whatShouldHappen: Loop i from 0 up to arr.length, advancing by i += 2.
patternExplanation: Advancing a loop index by chunk size k with .slice(i, i + k) partitions lists into fixed-size segments.

title: Array Fill: Fill Range with Value
description: Given an array arr, a value val, start index, and end index, return a new array copy where elements from start up to end are replaced using .fill(val, start, end).
patternExplanation: .fill() quickly replaces elements across a range with a static value.

title: Array copyWithin: Shift Subarray
description: Given an array arr, a target index, and a source start index, return a copy of arr after calling copyWithin(target, start).
patternExplanation: .copyWithin() transfers array sequences internally without altering array length.

title: Array Splice: Insert Element at Index
description: Given an array arr, an index, and an item, return a new array with item inserted at index using splice on a clone.
patternExplanation: Passing 0 as deleteCount to .splice(index, 0, item) inserts an element without overwriting existing items.

title: Array Splice: Replace Subarray Span
description: Given an array arr, start index, deleteCount, and replacement array newItems, return a new array where the span is replaced using splice.
patternExplanation: Using splice with both a deleteCount and replacement elements performs atomic in-place replacement.

title: Array Reverse: Create Inverted Array
description: Given an array arr, clone it and use .reverse() to return the reversed array without modifying the original input.
patternExplanation: Spreading [...arr] before calling .reverse() prevents unintended mutation of the input array.

title: Array Sort: By String Length
description: Given an array of strings words, return a new array sorted by string length ascending (shortest to longest).
patternExplanation: Using (a, b) => a.prop - b.prop sorts objects or strings based on a numerical attribute.

title: Array Sort: Users by Age
description: Given an array of user objects users where each object has name and age, return a new array sorted by age ascending.
whatShouldHappen: Clone users into a new array.
Sort using comparator (a, b) => a.age - b.age.
patternExplanation: Custom sort functions access object keys to arrange collection records cleanly.

title: Array Sort: Case-Insensitive Alphabetical
description: Given an array of strings words, return a sorted copy using a.localeCompare(b) so that sorting is case-insensitive.
patternExplanation: String.prototype.localeCompare() correctly handles linguistic sorting regardless of ASCII code point differences.

title: Array Sort: Booleans (False Before True)
description: Given an array of booleans bools, return a new array with false values sorted before true values.
patternExplanation: Coercing booleans to numbers (false -> 0, true -> 1) allows sorting flags via simple subtraction.

title: Array Sort: Strings Descending
description: Given an array of strings words, return a copy sorted in reverse alphabetical (descending) order using b.localeCompare(a).
patternExplanation: Inverting localeCompare arguments achieves descending lexicographical ordering.

title: Array Methods: Stack Simulation
description: Given an array of commands operations (strings like 'push:5' or 'pop'), simulate a stack starting empty. Return the final stack array.
whatShouldHappen: For each op, if op starts with "push:", push the extracted value to stack.
patternExplanation: Arrays implement LIFO (Last-In First-Out) stack operations via push() and pop().

title: Array Methods: FIFO Queue Simulation
description: Given an array of commands operations (strings like 'enqueue:X' or 'dequeue'), simulate a FIFO queue. Return the final queue array.
whatShouldHappen: If op starts with "enqueue:", push value to queue.
If op is "dequeue", shift() from queue.
patternExplanation: Arrays implement FIFO (First-In First-Out) queue semantics using push() for enqueue and shift() for dequeue.

title: Array Methods: Rotate Array Right by K
description: Given an array nums and integer k, rotate the array right by k steps using slice and concat without modifying nums.
whatShouldHappen: Slice last k items and concat with first length - k items.
patternExplanation: Combining slice(-k) and slice(0, length - k) with concat performs cyclic rotations in O(n) time.

title: Array Methods: Partition Even Numbers
description: Given an array nums, return a new array where all even numbers appear first, followed by all odd numbers, preserving relative order.
patternExplanation: Filtering two partitions and joining them with .concat() stabilizes ordered groupings.

title: Array Filter: Compact Falsy Values
description: Given an array arr containing mixed values, use Array.prototype.filter(Boolean) to remove all falsy values (0, false, null, undefined, NaN, "").
patternExplanation: Passing the Boolean constructor directly to .filter() strips all falsy values cleanly.

title: Array Filter: Unique Elements via IndexOf
description: Given an array arr, use arr.filter((val, idx, self) => self.indexOf(val) === idx) to return an array of unique values in first-seen order.
patternExplanation: If an element index matches self.indexOf(val), it is the first occurrence of that value in the array.

title: Array Filter: Intersection of Two Arrays
description: Given two arrays arr1 and arr2, use Array.prototype.filter and Array.prototype.includes to return elements of arr1 that exist in arr2.
patternExplanation: Filtering by collection inclusion computes the intersection of two arrays.

title: Array Filter: Difference of Two Arrays
description: Given two arrays arr1 and arr2, use arr1.filter(x => !arr2.includes(x)) to return elements that are in arr1 but NOT in arr2.
patternExplanation: Negating includes() inside filter computes the relative complement (A - B).

title: Array Filter: Symmetric Difference
description: Given two arrays arr1 and arr2, return all elements that are in either arr1 or arr2, but NOT in both.
whatShouldHappen: Find elements in arr1 not in arr2: diff1 = arr1.filter(x => !arr2.includes(x)).
Find elements in arr2 not in arr1: diff2 = arr2.filter(x => !arr1.includes(x)).
patternExplanation: Symmetric difference combines (A - B) and (B - A), isolating unique elements belonging exclusively to one array.

title: Array Map: Zip Two Arrays into Pairs
description: Given two arrays arr1 and arr2, return an array of pairs [[arr1[0], arr2[0]], [arr1[1], arr2[1]], ...] up to the length of the shorter array using .slice() and .map().
whatShouldHappen: Slice arr1 from 0 to min length.
patternExplanation: Zipping pairs corresponding elements from two collections by shared index.
